documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Initiative
documents.summary: University AI initiative page from the Provost office. It offers optional syllabus language that lets instructors set AI rules, requires documentation of any AI use, and assumes AI is disallowed when instructors are silent.
documents.stance_why: The page offers draft syllabus language, optional for faculty, saying instructors decide whether AI is allowed ('as determined by the instructor of the course'; 'Individual instructors may disallow'), with a fallback 'the student should assume that the use of such software is disallowed'. The university sets no uniform stance, so delegates.

units.why: The page says the initiative aims to 'leverage AI for student success'; it is an institution-level statement of purpose and scope for AI integration, so P56 (framework/preamble) fits rather than P44 since it is not about teaching students to use AI.
units.anchor: integrating AI into several areas of the university, from teaching to service delivery
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded P56/admin/general/informs on the opening scope and goal sentences (A anchored the scope clause, B the goal sentence). unit_stance differed (A encourage, B neutral). The source says the initiative aims 'to leverage AI for student success' and integrate AI into teaching, an institution-level endorsement of AI use, so encourage.

units.why: The committee 'monitors changing workforce needs in relation to AI', which ties the initiative to career preparation; this is an informational rationale, closest to P44.
units.anchor: The group monitors changing workforce needs in relation to AI.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase over-time, B general. The sentence 'The group monitors changing workforce needs in relation to AI' describes the initiative's remit and does not set a review or revision cycle for a policy, so general. Type P44, actor admin and informs agreed.

units.why: The committee 'introduces faculty to AI tools that may help streamline routine tasks'; this supports faculty in learning AI (P63), not a rule on how they use it (P59).
units.anchor: It also introduces faculty to AI tools that may help streamline routine tasks.

units.why: The committee examines 'ways to use AI to facilitate student learning, identify at-risk students earlier and increase student retention', an institutional commitment to use AI for learning and retention, which is a framework-level purpose (P56).
units.anchor: examines ways to use AI to facilitate student learning, identify at-risk students earlier
units.resolution_why: Matched: both P56/admin/general/informs. unit_stance encourage (both). A's topic codes retained (B's were not in the starter codebook).

units.why: The page provides 'suggested language regarding the use of AI in coursework' so faculty 'can easily add it to a syllabus'; this is a university-supplied syllabus template, P09, and the passage describes what the page offers rather than telling anyone to act, so informs.
units.anchor: included below is suggested language regarding the use of AI in coursework
units.frag_end: provide students with clarity about AI use in each course.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality should, B informs. The source ('included below is suggested language ... This will be sent to all faculty') states what the university provides and does not direct anyone; the recommendation to use it is the next sentence, coded separately. Final: informs. Actor admin, phase before-course and P09 agreed.

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged (but not required) to include the language below' is a soft recommendation that instructors put the university's AI statement in their syllabus, P09; 'encouraged' maps to should. Phase is course-start because the syllabus is how expectations reach students.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged (but not required) to include the language below.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase before-course, B course-start. The sentence concerns what goes into the syllabus that students receive, i.e. communicating expectations, so course-start. Actor instructor, modality should and P09 agreed.

units.why: 'Faculty are asked to clearly identify their expectations for AI use in each course they teach at the beginning of the course, including whether no use of AI is acceptable'; this asks every instructor to state AI expectations at course start, P09.
units.anchor: faculty are asked to clearly identify their expectations for AI use in each course
units.frag_end: whether no use of AI is acceptable.

units.why: The syllabus text says the university 'acknowledges that there are legitimate uses' of AI 'as determined by the instructor of the course'; the permission is not set by the university but handed to the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: legitimate uses of Artificial Intelligence, ChatBots, or other software
units.frag_end: determined by the instructor of the course.
units.policy: East Texas A&M University acknowledges legitimate uses of AI, ChatBots or other text-generating software, as determined by the instructor of the course.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B instructor. The passage is the university's own syllabus wording ('East Texas A&M University acknowledges ...') and is addressed to both students and instructors; the delegation to the instructor is the content, not the addressee. Final: all. Phase general, informs, P04, permit agreed.

units.why: The syllabus text defines the covered software as AI, chatbots or other software that 'generate text, or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words'; this scopes what the policy covers, P61.
units.anchor: capacity to generate text, or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The same sentence defines the covered software ('capacity to generate text, or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words'). This is a definition that scopes the policy, a real statement, so kept as P61 informs.

units.why: 'Any use of such software must be documented' requires students to document any AI use in the work, a disclosure rule (P24); no tool/prompt detail is demanded so not P25.
units.anchor: Any use of such software must be documented.
units.resolution_why: Actor, phase, modality, type agreed. unit_stance: A permit, B require. 'Any use of such software must be documented' makes disclosure mandatory; coded require (disclosure obligation) in line with the rest of the corpus.

units.why: 'Any undocumented use ... constitutes an instance of academic dishonesty (plagiarism)' makes nondisclosure itself the violation; P28 fits better than P36 because the violation hinges on failing to document, though it is also misconduct classification.
units.anchor: Any undocumented use of such software constitutes an instance of academic dishonesty (plagiarism).

units.why: 'Individual instructors may disallow entirely the use of such software for individual assignments or for the entire course' lets each instructor ban AI per assignment or course, which is P04.
units.anchor: Individual instructors may disallow entirely the use of such software

units.why: 'Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors' guidelines' tells students to follow each instructor's AI rules; it reflects per-instructor setting (P04), not a separate type for compliance.
units.anchor: Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors’ guidelines.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The source says 'Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors' guidelines', a separate sentence from the instructor-may-disallow rule and a distinct student duty. Kept as P04, student, course-start, should.

units.why: 'If no instructions are provided, the student should assume that the use of such software is disallowed' is the fallback rule when a syllabus is silent, P06.
units.anchor: the student should assume that the use of such software is disallowed

units.why: 'Students are fully responsible for the content of any assignment they submit, regardless of whether they used an AI' makes students own all submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: students are fully responsible for the content of any assignment they submit
units.frag_start: In any case, students are fully
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A neutral, B require. The sentence assigns responsibility for submitted work 'regardless of whether they used an AI' and does not take a position on whether to use AI, so neutral. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'This specifically includes cases in which the AI plagiarized another text or misrepresented sources' warns that AI output can plagiarize or misstate sources, and the student bears it; P31 (verify AI output) is nearest, though the text does not literally say verify.
units.anchor: cases in which the AI plagiarized another text or misrepresented sources

documents.unit: Research Integrity and Compliance (Academic Integrity Guide)
documents.title: Academic Integrity Guide: Faculty and Staff Information
documents.summary: Faculty section of the academic integrity guide. It tells instructors to state AI expectations, repeats that undocumented AI use is plagiarism and that silence means AI is disallowed, and asks faculty to meet students before reporting.
documents.stance_why: 'The instructor of the course determines legitimate uses' and 'Individual instructors may disallow', so the guide hands the decision to instructors despite the no-AI fallback.

units.why: The guide says 'acceptable use of AI in one class may count as cheating in another', i.e. a course's AI permission does not carry over, P11.
units.anchor: acceptable use of AI in one class may count as cheating in another
units.frag_start: AI is reshaping higher education, and
units.resolution_why: Matched; all codes agreed (P11, all, general, informs).

units.why: 'The instructor of the course determines legitimate uses' is a statement of who decides what AI use is legitimate, P04; it informs and sets a principle, so general, and it is delegation, not a position on AI.
units.anchor: The instructor of the course determines legitimate uses.
units.frag_start: East Texas A&M acknowledges that there
units.resolution_why: A coded phase before-course and unit_stance permit; B coded general and neutral. The sentence states a principle about who decides and takes no position on AI use itself, so general and neutral. Actor instructor, informs and P04 agreed.

units.why: The guide describes AI as 'chatbots, or other software that have the capacity to generate text or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words', defining the covered tools, P61.
units.anchor: capacity to generate text or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words
units.frag_start: East Texas A&M acknowledges that there
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The same passage defines the covered tools ('chatbots, or other software that have the capacity to generate text or suggest replacements for text beyond individual words'); a scope definition, kept as P61 informs.

units.why: 'Be clear with your students about acceptable uses of AI in your classes' directs faculty to communicate AI expectations, P09 (statement of expectations) rather than P10 which is for students.
units.anchor: Be clear with your students about acceptable uses of AI in your classes
units.frag_end: acceptable uses of AI in your classes

units.why: Faculty should 'consider how you might differentiate between acceptable uses of AI for various projects', encouraging per-assignment rules, P04.
units.anchor: consider how you might differentiate between acceptable uses of AI for various projects

units.why: 'Any use of AI software must be documented' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: Any use of AI software must be documented.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A permit, B require. 'Any use of AI software must be documented' is a mandatory disclosure rule; coded require as in the other documents. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'Any undocumented use of AI software constitutes academic dishonesty (plagiarism)' makes nondisclosure the violation, P28 chosen over P36 since the violation is the missing documentation.
units.anchor: Any undocumented use of AI software constitutes academic dishonesty (plagiarism).

units.why: 'Individual instructors may disallow the use of AI software for individual assignments or the entire course' gives instructors the right to ban AI, P04.
units.anchor: Individual instructors may disallow the use of AI software

units.why: 'Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors' guidelines' sends students to the instructor's rules, P04.
units.anchor: Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors' guidelines.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. 'Students should be aware of such requirements and follow their instructors' guidelines' is a student duty in the source that B skipped. Kept as P04, student, course-start, should.

units.why: 'If no AI guidelines are provided, the student should assume that the use of AI is disallowed' is the silent-syllabus fallback, P06.
units.anchor: the student should assume that the use of AI is disallowed

units.why: 'Students are fully responsible for the content of any assignment they submit, regardless of whether they used AI' is student ownership of submitted work, P29.

units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A neutral, B require. Responsibility for submitted work is not a position on AI use, so neutral. Other codes agreed.

units.anchor: This includes cases when AI plagiarized another text or misrepresented sources.

units.why: The guide says Turnitin is subscribed and faculty should 'encourage students to use it to avoid inaccurate resource citations and other forms of plagiarism'; this is a similarity-checking tool for plagiarism, P40, though it is not named as AI detection.

units.frag_end: forms of plagiarism in your classes.

documents.unit: Research Integrity and Compliance (Academic Integrity Guide)
documents.title: Academic Integrity Guide: Student Information
documents.summary: Student section of the academic integrity guide. It tells students AI rules vary by course, to ask the instructor first, to document any AI use, and to assume AI is not allowed if no guidelines are given.
documents.stance_why: 'Although using AI may be allowed in some courses or by some instructors, it is prohibited by others' and 'Talk with your course instructor before you use AI'; the stance is set per instructor, with a fallback of not allowed, so delegates.

units.why: 'Although using AI may be allowed in some courses or by some instructors, it is prohibited by others' states that rules vary by instructor, P04.
units.anchor: may be allowed in some courses or by some instructors, it is prohibited by others
units.frag_start: Although using AI may be allowed
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B student. The Student Guide addresses 'you' throughout and this sentence tells the student reader that rules differ by course and instructor, so student. Phase general, informs, P04 agreed.

units.why: 'Do not assume that the acceptable use of AI in one course applies to all others' is the course-specificity rule, P11.
units.anchor: acceptable use of AI in one course applies to all others
units.resolution_why: A coded must-not, B should-not. 'Do not assume that the acceptable use of AI in one course applies to all others' is a plain imperative prohibition on an assumption, so must-not. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'Talk with your course instructor before you use AI for any course assignment' tells students to ask the instructor before using AI on an assignment, P10 (student asks first); the trigger is using AI on assigned work, so during-work.
units.anchor: Talk with your course instructor before you use AI for any course assignment.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase course-start, B during-work. The duty is triggered by intending to use AI on a particular assignment, not by the start of the course, so during-work. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'Any use of AI software must be documented' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: Any use of AI software must be documented.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A permit, B require. 'Any use of AI software must be documented' is a mandatory disclosure rule, coded require. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'Any undocumented use of AI software constitutes academic dishonesty (plagiarism)' makes nondisclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Any undocumented use of AI software constitutes academic dishonesty (plagiarism).

units.why: 'Individual instructors may not allow the use of AI software for individual assignments or the entire course' lets instructors ban AI per assignment or course, P04.
units.anchor: Individual instructors may not allow the use of AI software
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B neutral. The sentence says instructors may set AI limits and does not itself restrict AI; the same instructor-may-disallow sentence is neutral in the other two documents. Neutral. Other codes agreed.

units.why: 'You should be aware of such requirements and follow your instructors' guidelines' sends students to instructor rules, P04.
units.anchor: You should be aware of such requirements and follow your instructors' guidelines.

units.why: 'If no AI guidelines are provided, you should assume that the use of AI is not allowed' is the silent-syllabus fallback, P06.
units.anchor: you should assume that the use of AI is not allowed
units.frag_end: use of AI is not allowed.

units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A neutral, B require. Responsibility for submitted work is not a position on AI use, so neutral. Other codes agreed.

notes: No school or computing-unit AI policy found; course documents deferred. All three documents are university-level and share one core AI text. Generic academic-integrity content that does not mention AI (misconduct definitions, reporting steps, sanctions, appeal, resource and workshop lists, procedure references) was not coded. Topic codes follow the starter codebook.
